The plotted value at age 1 is therefore 112 kg on the plate and 35 kg in the paragraph, and nothing on the page remarks on it. The asymptote 14.81 x 10^5 kg is 1481 tonnes, which the summary states as '14.8 x 10^5 kg' and which fixes the plate's ylim; the summary also says the dragon 'grew rapidly from age 3 to age 5' where the paragraph on this page says 'from 3 to 7 years old'. section_path: 5.1 The sensitivity analysis of dragon’s weight

note:
Paper 189, Team 1902727: the dragons of A Song of Ice and Fire, for problem A 2019. A logistic
mass-age fit, a Kleiber-law energy budget, a Malthus sheep flock, a Legendre-polynomial forage
regression over three climate regions, a seven-level ecosystem table, an NPP degradation model,
and a ten-offset sensitivity sweep. Twenty-four pages, fifteen measured regions, of which
fourteen are exhibits: SEVEN FIGURE ROWS and SEVEN TABLE ROWS, one refusal, nothing unaccounted.

THE MODEL'S TWO CONSTANTS DO NOT AGREE WITH THE MODEL. Equation (7) prints the Kleiber
coefficient as 4868598; substituting the paper's own equation (4) into equation (6) with q0 =
1926/0.7 gives 4366737, a ratio of 1.115. The same 1.115 appears again downstream: p11 carries
the flock scale as 296297 and the forage demand as 533335 kg/day, p13 carries 266609 and 479896
kg/day, and the two pairs differ by exactly that factor, so one of the two passages was written
with the other's constant. Neither passage says which.

THE LOGISTIC CANNOT PASS THROUGH ITS OWN DATA POINTS. The text fixes w(0)=10, w(1)=35 and
w(3)=14000 and then prints a three-parameter logistic. Solved exactly, those three constraints
have no real solution; the printed coefficients give w(1) = 112.45 kg, three times the stated
35 kg, and an asymptote of 1.481 million kg - 1481 tonnes, which the summary rounds to
'14.8 x 10^5 kg' and Figure 1 draws as a flat line from age 7. Figure 1 does draw the printed
logistic - digitized, the stroke sits within 0.03 x 10^5 of eq (4) evaluated at whole ages and
joined by straight chords, so between samples it departs from the smooth curve by at most about
0.9 x 10^5 - which means the 112 kg the plate shows at age 1 is the equation's value and the
35 kg is the prose's, and the large dragon clip art pasted over ages 2 to 9 hides the segment
where a reader would have noticed.

THE TWO SHEEP MODELS ARE ONE MODEL WITH TWO RATES. Equation (12) gives G = sm/(e^{b-d} - 1) with
the text's b-d = 0.0567, which would give G = 2880 and a negative breeding time; with b-d read
as a percentage, 0.000567, it gives G = 296212 and T = 16.4 years, which matches p11. p13's
266609 corresponds to b-d = 0.00063, i.e. to the assumptions page's 0.107% minus 0.044%, so the
paper switches from one rate to the other without a word and the two sheep counts, the two
forage demands and the two grassland areas all inherit the switch.

SEVEN OF THE FOURTEEN EXHIBITS ARE PRINTED TABLES, and the four plan views are drawn from the
same three numbers. Table 4 assigns seven ecosystems an assistance level 1 to 7 and a biomass;
Table 5 prints for the same seven the NPP and a biomass column that duplicates Table 4's exactly,
so the paper's one ecological data set is printed twice. Table 3's three areas imply forage
yields of 46859, 73517 and 36167 kg/(hm2 year) - between 3617 and 7352 g/(m2 year) - where
Table 5's own ceiling for the most productive ecosystem is 2200 g/(m2 year), so the three
regions the paper computes are two to three times more productive than any ecosystem in its own
table. Figure 6 draws the three areas as plan-view rectangles and the fourth panel as a single
red box labelled '100 Standard Olympic Track Field'; measured against Table 3 the drawn areas
are 0.72, 0.71 and 0.23 of the printed ones, so the ORDERING survives and the magnitudes do not.

THE SENSITIVITY SECTION IS TWO OFFSET GRIDS AND ONE FIGURE, and they do not cover the same
ground. Tables 6 and 7 print ten offsets, +5% to -5% in unit steps, over ages 1 to 7 and a
closing '>=8' column, all in per-cent deviation; Figure 7 prints only -3%, +3% and +0%, and
both its panels are titled 'Daily Intake(kcal)' although the caption promises a weight panel and
an intake panel. On the plate the +-3% curves do not straddle the baseline evenly - the right
panel's negative arm deviates about twice as far as its positive arm - and the two panels fan
differently from the same stated perturbation. Inside the grids the numbers are more orderly but
still anomalous: Table 6 gives +4% and -4% identical values at ages 2, 3 and 5 (4.52%, 3.79%,
4.19%), and Table 7 has -1% at age 3 printing 4.23% between 0.18% and 1.53%.

WHAT THE PAPER DOES WELL: every equation the exhibits rest on is printed with its number, the
two flow charts are correct dependency strips, the seven-level ecosystem ordering is stated in
one sentence and then used consistently, and the closing letter's four headline claims - 50+
sheep a day, 3738/2383/4843 hm2, 3.81 x 10^7 kg, 1.75 x 10^10 g of NPP - are each traceable to
a printed exhibit. The failures are internal: constants that do not propagate, a fit that cannot
produce its own points, and a sensitivity figure that answers a narrower question than its
caption asks.

Families: table-grid 7 (notation, Tables 2 to 7), line 4 (Figures 1, 2, 5, 7),
flowchart-or-schematic 2 (Figures 3, 4), map-or-plan-view 1 (Figure 6).
rules: Measure first, then read the pixels: fifteen measured regions over twenty-four pages resolve into seven figure rows, seven table rows and one refusal, with nothing unaccounted [place.doc_order].

The paper prints no Table 1: p13's prose cites 'table 1' for the integral regression model that is equation (16), and the only unnumbered grid is the notation block on p5, captioned by its own section heading [table.header_rows].

The mass-age figure draws the equation it prints but the equation contradicts the paper's own data: the curve follows the pasted logistic at yearly samples to within 0.03 x 10^5, while that logistic returns 112.45 kg at age 1 against the 35 kg the text states, and no real (wm, r0) satisfies w(0)=10, w(1)=35, w(3)=14000 at once [geometry.family].

The paper's own constants disagree by a factor of 1.115 in three places: equation (7)'s 4868598 against q0·wm^{3/4}/80^{3/4} = 4366737, and the two sheep counts 296297 (p11) against 266609 (p13) with their two forage demands 533335 and 479896 kg/day [table.text_cols].

Both sensitivity grids print ten offsets +5 to -5 and no 0% row, on a seven-column age grid closed by a '>=8' column, with the corner cell split diagonally between 'Age' and the offset label [table.diagonal_header].

Two of the four plan-view panels carry no area label at all, and all three labelled panels under-draw the areas Table 3 prints: arctic 34.8 against 48.43 km2, arid 26.5 against 37.38, temperate 5.46 against 23.83 [geometry.family].
Figure 7's caption promises a weight panel and a daily-intake panel, and both panels are labelled 'Daily Intake(kcal)' - no panel on the plate is titled Weight [caption.verbatim].

The notation grid's unit column is empty on four rows and inconsistent on two more: ni is g × year/m2 where the reduced quantity below it is g/year, and sm's unit day -1 is attached to a count [table.numeric_cols].

Two exhibits carry no sentence that names them - the notation grid, captioned only by its section heading, and Figure 5, whose citation is the deictic 'as shown in Figure 5' following a sentence about sensitivity indexes [mention.count].
The one region refused is the closing letter's addressee block, measured because the letter's header rules bracket it [place.page_zone].
Seven of the fourteen exhibits are printed tables, and the paper's only plan-view plate is drawn from the same three numbers the adjacent table prints [geometry.panel_count]

tables.note: Three columns - Abbreviation | Description | Unit - over twenty-seven body rows, ruled booktabs with no verticals, a rule above the first row and one at the foot. The symbol column is set in two conventions: plain italic for single letters (a, b, d, y, G), italic with a matching subscript for indexed forms (w(a), q(a), u(a), s(a), hi (t), xi (t), ci, Si, fi, Fi, ni), and a third treatment for the two derived deltas (∆N P P ij, ∆Fij) whose subscripts are set as loose capitals with the exponent notation broken up. FOUR ROWS CARRY NO UNIT AT ALL - G 'Scale of sheep flock under an ecological balance', g(t) 'The number of sheep after breeding for t days', g0 'Sensitive coefficient of forage yield' and xi (t) 'meteorological element' - and the two of them that the model later uses are used as the sheep-flock scale and as the initial flock, so the empty cells sit on quantities the arithmetic needs. g0 IS DEFINED AS THE WRONG QUANTITY: the row prints 'Sensitive coefficient of forage yield', but p10 writes 'let g0 be the initial number of sheep' and equation (13) sets g(0)=g0, so the table's one definition of g0 contradicts the model. sm IS TRUNCATED MID-SENTENCE - 'The number of sheep the three dragons' with no verb, and the printed unit day −1 belongs to a count, not to a rate. THE UNIT COLUMN IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: s(a) and b and d are counts of sheep, given day −1 and day −1; hi (t) is given kg/hm2 for a monthly yield and Yt kg/hm2 for a sum of eighteen regression terms; ni is given g × year/m2 where the same quantity is written g/year in ∆N P P ij two rows down; and ci is given kcal × day/m2, a unit the paper never uses again. The caption is the section heading itself - '3 Notation' printed above the grid with no 'Table 1' anywhere - so the table the paper calls Table 1 on p13 is not this one and no page identifies it. NO SENTENCE NAMES THE GRID.

mention.lead_sentence: the sensitivity indexes of herbage yield to temperature[6], precipitation[7] and sunshine[8] hours

tables.note: Four columns - 'Types of region' | Temperature | Rainfall | Sunshine hours - over three rows, arid, temperate and arctic, in a closed box with a rule between every row and a vertical rule between every column. THE BODY CELLS ARE NOT NUMBERS: each one is a Legendre expansion of degree three to five, keyed by a symbol - aT, aR, aS - that the header row does not explain, so the table is a coefficient list rather than a measurement table and cannot be read as a grid of values. THE HEADER AND THE BODY DISAGREE ON WHAT A COLUMN MEANS: the header names meteorological ELEMENTS (Temperature, Rainfall, Sunshine hours) while the cells are keyed by RESPONSE coefficients (aT, aR, aS), and the two readings only coincide because the column index and the subscript letter run together - the Temperature column is entirely aT, the Rainfall column entirely aR and the Sunshine column entirely aS, which is a layout convention the caption never states. THE CAPTION CALLS THE BODY SOMETHING ELSE AGAIN: it says 'sensitivity coefficient of monthly forage yield', and p11 defines that quantity hi (t) as a per-unit change in kg/hm2, whereas these cells are the coefficients aij of equation (17) - the fit, not the index - and the caption of the figure below says 'Change of sensitivity coefficients', using a third name for the same objects. ONE CELL IS A BARE HYPHEN: arid temperature has no expansion at all, so the paper fits two meteorological elements in the arid region and three in the other two, and no sentence says why - the omission is invisible in the surrounding text, which cites temperature[6] for the arid region on the very next page. THE COEFFICIENTS ARE PRINTED TO FOUR DIFFERENT PRECISIONS IN ONE COLUMN (1.681, 0.024, 0.122, 0.518; 2.8522 against 17.128; 4.6 with one digit against 21.723 with three), so the columns cannot be decimal-aligned even though they are all in the same units. The degree of each expansion differs by cell - five in the arid rainfall row, three in temperate, two in arctic - and the polynomial index set starts at phi0 in some cells and phi1 in others, so the pairs are not comparable term by term. Cited once by the sentence above it, which introduces the table as the output of a computation the paper calls 'successively calculated' and then never shows.

tables.note: Four columns - 'Types of region' | Arid | Temperate | Arctic - over two body rows, 'Grass yield (kg/hm2× year)' and 'Predation area (hm2)', in a closed box with rules between the rows and between the columns. The three yields are 33087.43, 42858.35 and 21085.43 and the three areas 3738.08, 2382.62 and 4843.12. THE TABLE IS THE PAPER'S ONE ARITHMETICALLY CHECKABLE EXHIBIT AND ITS OWN TWO ROWS DO NOT MULTIPLY OUT: yield times area gives 1.237e8, 1.021e8 and 1.021e8 kg/year, i.e. 338859, 279768 and 279779 kg/day, while the forage demand the paper states on p13 - 266609 sheep at 1.8 kg/day - is 479896 kg/day, so each region's printed area supports between 58 and 71 per cent of the flock the table exists to feed. Using the paper's earlier flock figure of 296297 sheep (533335 kg/day) the shortfall is larger still. The two rows are consistent only with each other if one divides the demand by the area, which implies yields of 46859, 73517 and 36167 kg/(hm2 year) - that is 4686, 7352 and 3617 g/(m2 year) - and those are 2.1, 3.3 and 1.6 times Table 5's own NPP ceiling of 2200 g/(m2 year) for tropical rain forest, the most productive ecosystem the paper lists; so whichever row is right, the yield row exceeds every natural ecosystem in the paper's own table. THE COLUMN ORDER IS NOT THE ORDER OF THE REGIONS IN THE PROSE: the table runs arid, temperate, arctic, the text of 4.3.3 introduces 'arid, warm and polar', the caption of the figure below says 'different climates', and Figure 5's legend says Egypt, Australia and Iceland; 'warm' and 'temperate' are never equated, and neither are 'polar' and 'arctic'. THE ROW LABEL'S UNIT IS BROKEN: 'kg/hm2× year' puts the multiplication sign between the area and the year without a space, so the quantity reads as kilograms per hectare-times-year rather than per hectare per year, and the area row is in hm2 with no per-anything. THE YIELDS CARRY TWO DECIMALS AND THE AREAS TWO, uniformly, which is the one place in the paper where a column is printed to a consistent precision. Cited twice on its own page - once by the lead-in that introduces it as the output of section 4.3.2 and once by 'Combined with Table 3 and Figure 6', the sentence that draws the region ranking from it.

mention.lead_sentence: Looking at the relevant data, we can get the average biomass per unit area of different ecosystems, as shown in Table 4.

tables.note: Four columns - Type of ecosystem | Level of assistance | Specie richness | Average biomass fi(kg/m2) - over seven ecosystems in a closed grid with a rule between every row, the caption above the header. As printed the seven rows descend by species richness: tropical rain forest at level 1 with biomass 45, temperate evergreen broad-leaved forest at 2 with 35, swamp and wetland at 3 with 12.3, savanna at 4 with 4, temperate grassland at 5 with 1.6, desert at 6 with 0.6 and ice sheet at 7 with 0.02. THE TWO VALUE COLUMNS ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF NUMBER: the level column is an ordinal position from 1 to 7 assigned by the prose ('corresponding to 7 assistance levels, from high to low are recorded as Level 1, Level 2, Level 3...'), and it runs in the same direction as the biomass column, so the best-supported ecosystem carries the lowest level number - the opposite of what 'level of assistance' reads as, and the paper never says which way the scale runs. THE BIOMASS COLUMN IS PRINTED TO WILDLY VARYING PRECISION: 45 and 35 are integers, 12.3, 1.6 and 0.6 carry one decimal, 4 carries none and 0.02 carries two, so the column cannot be decimal-aligned and the ratio between the largest and smallest entries is 2250. 'Specie richness' is printed as a word in the header with NO VALUES BENEATH IT - the column has a heading and no cells - so the ordering the table is built on is asserted in the header and not shown in the grid; and the prose's justification ('the higher the species richness of the ecosystem, the higher the level of aid') cannot be checked against a single printed richness figure. The unit kg/m2 appears in the header with the symbol's subscript broken off, and no row labels the ecosystem by climate region, so the connection to Table 3's arid / warm / polar is left to the body text, which asserts it on p16 ('The temperate grassland corresponds to the level 5 assitance'). Cited twice on its own page.

tables.note: Three columns - the ecosystem name, 'Average NPP(g/m2× year)' and 'Average biomass(kg/m2)' - over the same seven ecosystems in the same order and the same closed grid as Table 4: tropical rain forest 2200 and 45, temperate evergreen broad-leaved forest 1300 and 35, swamp and wetland 2000 and 12.3, savanna 900 and 4, temperate grassland 600 and 1.6, desert 140 and 0.6, ice sheet 3 and 0.02. THE BIOMASS COLUMN IS TABLE 4'S BIOMASS COLUMN REPEATED DIGIT FOR DIGIT, two pages apart, with no cross-reference and no note - so the paper prints one data set twice and the second printing is what equations (23) and (24) draw their f values from, which at least makes the two consistent by construction. THE NPP COLUMN IS THE ONE NEW DATA SET IN THE PAPER, and its ORDER IS NOT THE ORDER OF EITHER OF THE TABLE'S OTHER TWO COLUMNS: swamp and wetland takes 2000 g/(m2 year) - second only to the rain forest and above the temperate forest's 1300 - while its biomass is 12.3, a quarter of the forest's 35; so the table pairs a high-productivity, low-standing-stock ecosystem with its neighbours and the paper reads the two columns as if they ordered the same way. THE UNITS ARE SET THREE WAYS IN ONE HEADER ROW: 'g/m2× year' with a multiplication sign and no space before it, 'kg/m2' with none, and the ecosystem column with no unit at all. THE PAPER'S OWN WORKED EXAMPLE DOES NOT USE THE ROW IT NAMES: p17 computes 'ecosystem types for Temperate evergreen forest ... degrade into Temperate grasslands' and substitutes (1300 - 600) and (35 - 1.6), which are the rows the table numbers 2 and 5 - both printed correctly - but the model's degradation pair is then asserted for a forest the table never identifies by latitude or climate. Cited by the sentence above it with the pointer set in lower case ('shown in table 5').

tables.note: Eight columns - 'Weight Offset' then ages 1 to 7 with a closing '>=8' column - over ten rows of offsets +5% to -5% in unit steps, ten-by-eight in a closed grid with a rule between every row. THE CORNER CELL IS SPLIT DIAGONALLY holding 'Age' above the diagonal and 'Weight Offset' below it, so the row header and the column header are one cell. THE GRID HAS TEN ROWS AND NO ZERO ROW: +5, +4, +3, +2, +1, -1, -2, -3, -4, -5, with the unperturbed case the figure two pages earlier plots as '+0%' printed nowhere, so the baseline the deviations are deviations FROM is not in the table. TRANSCRIBED: +5% 5.37 6.09 6.87 7.42 7.30 9.86 8.42 6.44; +4% 4.37 4.52 3.79 2.87 4.19 6.27 6.03 5.42; +3% 2.15 1.78 2.36 2.44 2.89 4.27 5.02 5.36; +2% 2.13 2.35 3.48 4.62 4.35 3.52 4.07 4.35; +1% 0.02 0.01 0.01 0.18 1.18 2.03 2.15 2.17; -1% 0.07 0.09 0.19 0.19 2.30 2.39 2.78 3.05; -2% 1.03 1.27 1.98 2.37 2.05 3.40 3.57 3.92; -3% 2.33 1.54 2.88 2.97 3.23 3.89 4.12 5.22; -4% 3.33 4.52 3.79 3.60 4.19 7.23 6.58 6.72; -5% 6.28 5.40 3.21 8.32 8.54 11.23 9.87 8.40. NO COLUMN IS MONOTONE IN THE OFFSET, in either direction: at age 5 the +2% row prints 4.35 against the +3% row's 2.89, and the +4% row's 4.19 against the +5% row's 7.30; the +1% row is the column minimum at every one of the eight ages, so the smallest perturbation gives the smallest deviation on both signs and the response is not smooth through zero. TWO ROWS ARE IDENTICAL CELL BY CELL where they should differ: +4% and -4% print the same values at ages 2 (4.52), 3 (3.79) and 5 (4.19), three of eight columns. ONE CELL IS OUT OF FAMILY: -5% at age 3 prints 3.21% where its own row runs 5.40 and 8.32 on either side and every -2, -3 and -4 value in that column is higher. NO CELL CARRIES A UNIT: the caption's 'deviation' is not defined as a percentage of weight or of the age-1 weight, and the + signs on the positive rows and the bare digits on the negative rows are the only indication of direction. The caption prints ABOVE, and the grid carries no note.

ONE CELL IS WILDLY OUT OF FAMILY: -1% at age 3 prints 4.23% between 0.18% and 1.53% on its own row, and -5% at age 3 prints 3.90% between 8.62% and 9.34% on its own row, so the age-3 column holds two numbers that belong to neither neighbouring offset nor to their own row. THE TWO GRIDS DISAGREE ABOUT WHICH ROW IS THE OUTLIER: -5% is the column maximum at seven of the eight ages in Table 6 and at only five of eight here, and the +5% row is the column maximum at ages 3, 6, 7 and in the closing '>=8' column here against only ages 2 and 3 there. The +1% row is the column minimum at all eight ages in Table 6 and at five of eight here, so the smallest perturbation gives the smallest deviation on both signs without exception in the weight grid and with three exceptions in the intake grid. NO ROW OR COLUMN SUMS, no baseline row exists, and no cell carries a unit. Both grids are named in one sentence, which is the only sentence either has.
